title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and contract modifications, while NASA's lunar ambitions face a reality check. Meanwhile, the defense sector is increasingly entwined with AI, as companies pivot to meet emerging threats.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space
themes.body: Iceye's hefty €1 billion raise and Isar Aerospace's €270 million boost highlight a growing appetite for investment in satellite systems and launch capabilities. This trend suggests that the space economy is maturing, attracting serious capital for ambitious projects.

themes.title: NASA's Moon Base Woes
themes.body: New Glenn's recent setbacks have forced NASA to rethink its lunar base plans, underscoring the complexities of ambitious space architecture. As timelines slip, stakeholders are reminded that the path to the Moon is rarely a straight line.

themes.title: AI's Defense Surge
themes.body: With every startup seemingly pivoting to 'AI for Defense', the sector is witnessing a significant shift towards integrating advanced technologies into military applications. This trend could reshape operational strategies, but the long-term viability remains to be seen.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions in Orbit
themes.body: Increased Russian co-orbital activity near commercial GEO slots raises eyebrows and highlights the ongoing geopolitical chess game in space. As nations vie for dominance, the implications for commercial operations could be profound.
